title: Introduce predictive KV prefetch proxy and scheduler demurrer
creator: Sofia Kim
description: Background: Over the last year we've accumulated multiple point fixes around prefetch and slot admission that reduce tail latency but increase code complexity and coupling between the scheduler and KV cache. This ticket refactors the prefetch path into a lightweight predictive prefetch proxy and isolates a small scheduler 'demurrer' component to reduce lock contention and allow independent scaling and testing. Goal: reduce median and P95 tail latency variance under bursty workloads, decrease scheduler lock hold times by 30-50%, and simplify the KV warmup contract for downstream teams.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a predictive prefetch proxy that sits between admission and KV adapter with a stable contract and documented API
Scheduler demurrer extracted as a single-threaded event loop component with explicit handoff points and no global scheduler lock during prefetch decisions
End-to-end tests validate cache correctness (no miss regressions) and memory usage stays within current baselines +/-5% under load test profiles
Benchmarks show scheduler critical-section hold time reduced by >=30% on our synthetic spike workload
Canary rollout plan executed without increased 5xxs or client-visible latency regressions; rollback plan validated
Code reviewed and merged, with runtime-1.22 release note and migration doc published
implementation_notes: Design: predictive prefetch proxy maintains a compact LRU + exponential backoff per-session heuristic; avoids touching full KV shard metadata during hot admission bursts
API: define Proxy.prefetch(session_id, token_prefix, hint_score) -> prefetch_handle opaque token; prefetch_handle supports cancel() to stop work if request is served from cache
Scheduler: extract 'demurrer' event loop to evaluate admission window and defer non-critical prefetch decisions off the main admission fast path
Telemetry: emit histograms for demurrer_loop_duration_ms, prefetch_queue_depth, prefetch_hit_ratio, and kv_eviction_pressure
Testing: unit tests for proxy eviction semantics, integration tests with slot prewarmer (ENG-33109) and admission metrics, chaos tests for demurrer unavailability
Rollout: staged canary - 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with automatic rollback on increased retry rates or spike in tail latency
Docs: migration guide describing how custom admission plugins should call the new proxy; deprecation timeline for old prefetch helpers (2 releases)
